sources.entry: OpenPost | Self-hosted social publishing and scheduling platform with Docker Compose support

summary.one_liner: OpenPost is an open-source, self-hostable social media publishing and scheduling app that also includes image and video editors, positioned as an alternative to Buffer, Canva, and CapCut.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a workspace for connecting social accounts (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, YouTube, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Pixelfed, PeerTube, Lemmy, PieFed, Discord, Pinterest, Telegram) and composing per-platform posts with previews. It offers a calendar and publishing queues, visual workflows that turn GitHub releases, RSS feeds, or prompts into drafts, and auto-repost rules for supported networks. It includes a media library, a meme maker, an inbox for supported comments and DMs, analytics, and optional AI writing. A browser-based image editor (carousels, layers, background removal) and a multitrack video editor with a screen recorder are also described. An API, TypeScript SDK, CLI, MCP support, and n8n integration are listed. The self-host option runs via Docker Compose with SQLite and local media storage by default.
use_cases: schedule social media posts across accounts
design social media carousels and thumbnails
automate posts from GitHub releases or RSS feeds
manage brand and client accounts in separate workspaces
reply to comments and DMs in one inbox
how_to_run: Run OpenPost with Docker Compose (default setup: one container with SQLite and local media storage)
See the README's Self-host guide and 'Configure integrations' docs for setup details
Review 'Backups and upgrades' docs before upgrading
notable: Combines social scheduling with image carousel design and multitrack video editing in one app
Workflow canvas that turns GitHub releases, RSS feeds, and prompts into reviewed drafts
Self-hosted with a default single-container Docker Compose setup using SQLite
Exposes API, TypeScript SDK, CLI, MCP, and n8n integration for scripts and agents
caveats: Hosted signups are currently on a waitlist while social platform approvals are finished
Some integrations require provider app approval or publicly reachable media URLs
Posting formats, inbox features, and analytics vary by platform; Mastodon and Pixelfed connect per instance
